issue.title: `&FM_DIAG_SETTINGS` seems to have no effect since 2023: should these settings reach the redistribution again?
issue.body:
While experimenting with block sizes and rank counts for the diagonalization of large BSE matrices, I tried `&GLOBAL &FM_DIAG_SETTINGS`, and none of its keywords seemed to change anything. Looking into it, it seems to me that `cp_fm_redistribute_init` stores the four values and then overwrites them with a default-constructed structure:

https://github.com/cp2k/cp2k/blob/79559d0e103e48aba86c1dd5d95e441a4b2f717a/src/fm/cp_fm_diag_utils.F#L155-L166

and that `cp_fm_redistribute_work_finalize` does the same after every redistribution:

https://github.com/cp2k/cp2k/blob/79559d0e103e48aba86c1dd5d95e441a4b2f717a/src/fm/cp_fm_diag_utils.F#L137-L138

If I read the history correctly, the settings survived from their introduction in cd4030cbb5 (2018) on, because the call after the assignments, `cp_fm_redistribute_work_init`, only reset the communicator and the pointers. With the refactoring in 3c1a8767f5432c037bf6c68b63f89bb625f1557b (2023-02-13), the type got default values (`a = x = -1`, both flags `.FALSE.`) and both calls became the structure constructor, which resets every component. Since then the code seems to run with these defaults, whatever the input says:

https://github.com/cp2k/cp2k/blob/79559d0e103e48aba86c1dd5d95e441a4b2f717a/src/fm/cp_fm_diag_utils.F#L60-L70

### What I have seen

- **ScaLAPACK:** as far as I can tell, the optimal rank count comes out as `-K` for a matrix of order `K`, so every matrix is marked for redistribution ([L174-L181](https://github.com/cp2k/cp2k/blob/79559d0e103e48aba86c1dd5d95e441a4b2f717a/src/fm/cp_fm_diag_utils.F#L174-L181), [L366-L367](https://github.com/cp2k/cp2k/blob/79559d0e103e48aba86c1dd5d95e441a4b2f717a/src/fm/cp_fm_diag_utils.F#L366-L367)). The partition `[-K, num_pe + K]` then does not pass the check in `mp_comm_split`, which falls back to an even split ([message_passing.F#L2761-L2772](https://github.com/cp2k/cp2k/blob/79559d0e103e48aba86c1dd5d95e441a4b2f717a/src/mpiwrap/message_passing.F#L2761-L2772)). So every ScaLAPACK diagonalization seems to run on half the ranks, with two `pdgemr2d` copies.
- **ELPA:** `ELPA_FORCE_REDISTRIBUTE` always ends up `.FALSE.` ([L331-L348](https://github.com/cp2k/cp2k/blob/79559d0e103e48aba86c1dd5d95e441a4b2f717a/src/fm/cp_fm_diag_utils.F#L331-L348)), while #1515 made `.TRUE.` the documented default.
- **Output:** `PRINT_FM_REDISTRIBUTE` does not print anything either.

A minimal check: four water molecules, DZVP-MOLOPT-SR-GTH (order 92), four SCF steps, 4 ranks, ScaLAPACK, `PRINT_FM_REDISTRIBUTE T`. On current master, settings that should behave differently give the same energy to every printed digit and print nothing:

| `&FM_DIAG_SETTINGS` | master | settings in effect (branch below) |
|---|---|---|
| defaults (`PARAMETER_A 4`, `PARAMETER_X 60`) | -68.660740559939200, no `CP_FM_DIAG` output | -68.660740559939214, not redistributed |
| `PARAMETER_A -1`, `PARAMETER_X -1` | -68.660740559939200, no output | -68.660740559939200, target -92 |
| `PARAMETER_A 1`, `PARAMETER_X 1` | -68.660740559939200, no output | -68.660740559939214, not redistributed |

Master always gives the value of the `-1` row. With the settings in effect, the redistribution report shows what each setting does. In the table below, the *today* rows set `PARAMETER_A -1`, `PARAMETER_X -1` (or `ELPA_FORCE_REDISTRIBUTE F`), which reproduces master, so the print shows the decisions master takes:

| ranks | library | settings | optimal CPUs | diagonalized on | total energy (Ha) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | ScaLAPACK | in effect | 4 | 4 ranks | -68.660740559939214 |
| 4 | ScaLAPACK | today | -92 | 2 ranks (even split) | -68.660740559939200 |
| 8 | ScaLAPACK | in effect | 4 | 4 ranks | -68.660740559939214 |
| 8 | ScaLAPACK | today | -92 | 4 ranks (even split) | -68.660740559939214 |
| 8 | ELPA | in effect (`.TRUE.`) | 4 | 4 ranks | -68.660740559939185 |
| 8 | ELPA | today (`.FALSE.`) | 4 | 8 ranks | -68.660740559939185 |

### Where I missed having the tuning knobs as input variables

- **Memory.** A 275176 x 275176 BSE matrix on 480 ranks (ScaLAPACK) died with `xxmr2d: out of memory` inside the split. With the settings in effect it would not be redistributed at all (`ceil(K/240)*4 > 480`), but I found no input that avoids the split today.
- **Small matrices on many ranks.** Here a smaller grid is often faster, and these settings would be the way to ask for one. On one node with 32 ranks, a K = 4140 ScaLAPACK case goes from 1.394 s (2 redistributions, 3.211 GB per rank) to 1.181 s (none, 3.180 GB). With ELPA on 64 ranks and matrices of order 216 to 2448 (median target 16 ranks), the solves ran 2.46x faster, though the redistributions gave back 75 % of that gain.

### What makes me unsure how to proceed

Letting the settings take effect again is a small change, but it switches on behaviour that has not run since 2023:

- **The heuristic is not always a win.** K = 1472 on 32 ranks (ScaLAPACK) gets slower, 0.198 s to 0.235 s.
- **`ELPA_FORCE_REDISTRIBUTE .TRUE.` becomes active.** Time of `cp_fm_diag_elpa`, `.TRUE.` over `.FALSE.`:

  | ranks -> heuristic target | 32 -> 32 | 32 -> 28 | 32 -> 16 | 32 -> 4 | 64 -> 16 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | T/F | 1.00 | **1.46** | 0.88, 0.90 | 0.99 | 0.85 |

  In a development version of an iterative BSE solver (dense matrices of a few hundred rows on 32 ranks via `choose_eigv_solver`), a non-default `PARAMETER_X 30` with the flag `.TRUE.` aborted in 2 of 3 runs with `ELPA [pre-fail]: Problem contains processor column with zero width.` ([cp_fm_elpa.F#L403](https://github.com/cp2k/cp2k/blob/79559d0e103e48aba86c1dd5d95e441a4b2f717a/src/fm/cp_fm_elpa.F#L403)). The last report before the aborts read order 509 (536), optimal CPUs 20, maximum CPUs with non-zero columns 32, so the guard passed; as far as I can see it is evaluated before the grid and the block size change. `PARAMETER_X` 60 or 120, or the flag `.FALSE.`, ran clean (9 of 9).
- **Reference values move.** In the 2-rank regression tests every ScaLAPACK diagonalization then runs on 2 ranks instead of 1. Compared with master built the same way on the same node, three tests leave their tolerance:

  | test | master | settings in effect | reference, tolerance |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `QS/regtest-tddfpt-force-libxc/h2o_lda_analytic` | -17.12647009 | -17.12646999 | -17.12647008678879, 1e-11 |
  | `QMMM/QS/regtest-cdft/HeH-water-mixed-cdft-1` | -0.14475142 | -0.1447478609 | -0.144751419983, 5e-10 |
  | `QMMM/QS/regtest-cdft/HeH-water-mixed-cdft-2` | -0.1447514199 | -0.1447478609 | -0.144751419983, 5e-10 |

  The CDFT pair also varies between nodes: on a compute node `-1` passed and `-2` read -0.1447514266. Four more tests fail on this machine with and without the change, so I assume they are unrelated.

### Questions

1. Is it expected that `&FM_DIAG_SETTINGS` currently has no effect? Did I maybe miss how to correctly set these parameters?
2. Would it make sense to let these settings take effect again? If so, is the [branch](https://github.com/MGraml/cp2k/commit/bb6330448f2e82573c30efe1ee3b861ccc1e8d5e) i also link below below a reasonable way to do it?
3. Which `ELPA_FORCE_REDISTRIBUTE` default would be good given the numbers above?
4. Or would a different approach fit better, for example revisiting the redistribution heuristic?
A possible change is on a branch of my fork. It restores the pre-2023 behaviour, keeps every documented default and touches only `cp_fm_diag_utils.F`:

https://github.com/MGraml/cp2k/commit/bb6330448f2e82573c30efe1ee3b861ccc1e8d5e

(compare with master: https://github.com/cp2k/cp2k/compare/master...MGraml:cp2k:fix_fm_diag_settings_clobber)

If it helps, I am happy to turn it into a PR. Since I am not too familiar with these code parts, I would be happy about any suggestions/ideas.

All the best,
Max





<details><summary>The same change as a diff</summary>

```diff
    SUBROUTINE cp_fm_redistribute_work_finalize(has_redistributed)
 ...
-      ! Return work to its initial state
-      work_redistribute = cp_fm_redistribute_type()
+      NULLIFY (work_redistribute%group_distribution)
+      NULLIFY (work_redistribute%group_partition)
+      NULLIFY (work_redistribute%blacs_env_new)
+      NULLIFY (work_redistribute%para_env_new)

    SUBROUTINE cp_fm_redistribute_init(a, x, should_print, elpa_force_redistribute)
 ...
+      work_redistribute = cp_fm_redistribute_type()
       work_redistribute%a = a
       work_redistribute%x = x
       work_redistribute%should_print = should_print
       work_redistribute%elpa_force_redistribute = elpa_force_redistribute
-      ! Init work
-      work_redistribute = cp_fm_redistribute_type()
```
</details>

<details><summary>Minimal deck (ScaLAPACK row; the others change `&FM_DIAG_SETTINGS` or the library)</summary>

```
&GLOBAL
  PROJECT fmdiag
  RUN_TYPE ENERGY
  PRINT_LEVEL MEDIUM
  PREFERRED_DIAG_LIBRARY SCALAPACK
  &FM_DIAG_SETTINGS
    PRINT_FM_REDISTRIBUTE T
  &END FM_DIAG_SETTINGS
&END GLOBAL
&FORCE_EVAL
  METHOD QS
  &DFT
    BASIS_SET_FILE_NAME BASIS_MOLOPT
    POTENTIAL_FILE_NAME GTH_POTENTIALS
    &QS
      EPS_DEFAULT 1.0E-10
    &END QS
    &MGRID
      CUTOFF 200
    &END MGRID
    &SCF
      MAX_SCF 4
      IGNORE_CONVERGENCE_FAILURE T
      EPS_SCF 1.0E-3
      SCF_GUESS ATOMIC
      &DIAGONALIZATION
        ALGORITHM STANDARD
      &END DIAGONALIZATION
    &END SCF
    &XC
      &XC_FUNCTIONAL PBE
      &END XC_FUNCTIONAL
    &END XC
  &END DFT
  &SUBSYS
    &CELL
      ABC 10.0 10.0 10.0
    &END CELL
    &COORD
      O   0.000  0.000  0.000
      H   0.757  0.586  0.000
      H  -0.757  0.586  0.000
      O   3.500  0.000  0.000
      H   4.257  0.586  0.000
      H   2.743  0.586  0.000
      O   0.000  3.500  0.000
      H   0.757  4.086  0.000
      H  -0.757  4.086  0.000
      O   0.000  0.000  3.500
      H   0.757  0.586  3.500
      H  -0.757  0.586  3.500
    &END COORD
    &KIND O
      BASIS_SET DZVP-MOLOPT-SR-GTH
      POTENTIAL GTH-PBE-q6
    &END KIND
    &KIND H
      BASIS_SET DZVP-MOLOPT-SR-GTH
      POTENTIAL GTH-PBE-q1
    &END KIND
  &END SUBSYS
&END FORCE_EVAL
```
</details>

Setup: Noctua 2 (192 cores per node), GCC, OpenMPI, OpenBLAS, ScaLAPACK, ELPA 2024.05.001, master `79559d0e10`. Related: #578, #1444, #1515, #3069.
